forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Barking Power accounts not prepared as going concern; City's Estate letter of support required
news_drafts.lead:
The external auditor's 2026 audit findings report on City's Estate says the accounts of Barking Power Ltd are prepared on a basis other than going concern, meaning not on the assumption that the company will keep operating. (An external audit is an independent check on the accounts.) The report is Appendix 3a to the papers for the City of London's Audit and Risk Management Committee, which meets on 2 November 2026.

The auditor writes that "a letter of support from City Estate is required to confirm that it intends to provide funding for the power station". According to the report, the letter must confirm that City's Estate will fund the power station. It must also confirm that City's Estate will not recall intercompany loans or balances, the money owed between companies in the same group, before decommissioning of the power station is complete.

Apart from Barking Power, the auditor reports nothing that brings the Group's going concern assumption into question. The paper gives no figures for the support the letter would cover.

news_drafts.headline: City of London Police forecasts £1.66m underspend on £126.0m budget, helped by £6.8m in pay savings
news_drafts.lead:
City of London Police is forecasting that it will spend £1.66m less than its budget this year, according to first-quarter budget monitoring (the in-year check of spending against budget) reported to the City of London Police Authority Board on 14 October. The underspend is 1.3% of a £126.0m budget.

The papers attribute most of it to £6.8m of savings on workforce pay. Recruitment delays and lower staffing than budgeted meant the money set aside for officers and staff exceeded actual costs, even with what the paper calls significant recruitment activity. Officer and staff numbers remain below budgeted levels. The pay underspends have been used to cover cost pressures arising during the year.

The papers say the position "remains dependent upon temporary vacancy-related savings which are expected to reduce as recruitment progresses". They add that the savings "are not expected to be sustainable in the longer term". The force says it needs to review its cost pressures through the 2027/28 budget-setting process.

findings.paper_title: Internal Audit Update November 2026 Appendix 1 - IA Dashboard Q2
findings.headline: Cyclical Works Programme audit rated Substantial, with its one recommendation on project prioritisation records closed as implemented
findings.detail: The audit confirmed governance, cost management, performance monitoring and reporting operating effectively across the Cyclical Works Programme, with effective budgetary control. The single improvement related to documenting prioritisation and sequencing decisions, and management's action plan has been accepted as implemented.
findings.matters: Confirmed budgetary control and closed remediation on a capital maintenance programme give peers a documented example of programme-level cost control.
findings.figures: Assurance rating: Substantial; 1 amber recommendation, now closed as implemented
findings.quote: the recommendation is closed as implemented.

findings.paper_title: Internal Audit Update November 2026 Appendix 1 - IA Dashboard Q2
findings.headline: Veolia Cleansing Contract audit rated Moderate, with the contract described as generally well managed and recurring KPI underperformance flagged for root-cause analysis
findings.detail: The audit found clear governance, defined accountability and structured performance monitoring in place for the Veolia Cleansing Contract. It also identified an opportunity to strengthen root-cause analysis where KPI failures persist, and to ensure decision-makers are aware of long-term performance when considering contract extension.
findings.matters: Contract extension decisions on a significant waste service that rest on long-term performance information are a live decision point for councils managing similar large operational contracts.
findings.figures: Assurance rating: Moderate; 1 red, 1 amber and 1 green recommendation
findings.quote: the contract is generally well managed

findings.paper_title: Internal Audit Update November 2026 Appendix 1 - IA Dashboard Q2
findings.headline: Financial Framework Mapping audit rated Moderate, with progress on the financial framework documentation described as having slowed
findings.detail: The audit found Financial Regulations well maintained and alignment with the CIPFA Financial Management Code, Prudential Code and Accounting Code strong, but detailed requirements are dispersed across policies with no single repository. It attributes slowing progress to competing priorities and capacity pressures from Programme Sapphire and Ambition 25.
findings.matters: A council whose financial control framework is fragmented and slowing under programme capacity pressure is a point of comparison for finance officers running similar transformation programmes.
findings.figures: Assurance rating: Moderate; 2 amber recommendations; 0 red recommendations
findings.quote: progress appears to have slowed because of competing priorities

findings.paper_title: Internal Audit Update November 2026 Appendix 1 - IA Dashboard Q2
findings.headline: Instructing Legal Advice audit, rated Substantial, finds the Corporation has no mechanism to identify breaches of Standing Orders where departments instruct external counsel directly
findings.detail: The audit found commissioning through the Comptroller and City Solicitor well controlled, but wider work identified departments and institutions directly instructing external legal advice without engaging the Comptroller and City Solicitor's Department. Recommendations include clarifying that only the City Comptroller may appoint external counsel and exploring a system control requiring CCS Legal approval before legal-coded purchase requisitions can be raised.
findings.matters: Uncontrolled external legal spend and procurement outside central approval is a control gap that finance directors at other councils are likely to test for in their own procurement frameworks.
findings.figures: 1 amber and 1 green recommendation; 0 red recommendations
findings.quote: There are no mechanisms in place to identify, monitor and review

findings.paper_title: Internal Audit Update November 2026 Appendix 1 - IA Dashboard Q2
findings.headline: Barbican Centre business continuity recommendations are 561 days past their original dates, with Committee intervention recorded in the paper
findings.detail: Ten business continuity recommendations for the Barbican Centre meet both intervention triggers: at least one year past the original due date and three or more follow-ups. The paper records that the Barbican Finance and Risk Committee intervention has already taken place, and the recommended approach is to monitor.
findings.matters: Overdue business continuity remediation at a major cultural and events venue is a resilience and governance exposure that other councils running similar arm's-length or trading operations will track.
findings.figures: 561 days past original date; 10 recommendations meeting both triggers; 3 recommendations meeting one trigger; 3 High and 8 Medium and 2 Low across the committee list
findings.quote: The oldest recommendations are 561 days past their original dates.
